chunks: And from him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the crops from which zakat is due, and he said: 'Wheat, barley, millet, rice, salt, and lentils; all of these are from that which zakat is due.'
And he said: 'Everything that is measured by the sa' and reaches the awsan (thresholds), upon it is zakat.'

And whatever runs in their manner from that which entails the obligation of zakat upon it, then it is considered recommended and preferred rather than obligatory and mandatory. And we said this so that the reports do not contradict each other, and because in what we mentioned earlier from the reports, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pardoned what is other than that. And if these items were among that which zakat is obligatory upon, they would not be pardoned. And that which clarifies what we mentioned and makes it clear is that they did not say that there is zakat in these items in the manner of obligation and mandatory duty.
ai.seo_question: Which agricultural crops are subject to obligatory zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific agricultural commodities subject to obligatory zakat, establishing the criteria of measurement by the *sa'* and reaching the *awsaq* threshold. Shaykh al-Tusi employs the principle of *jam'* (reconciliation) to resolve apparent contradictions in hadith, distinguishing between strict obligation (*wajib*) for these primary crops and recommendation (*mandub*) for others, thereby preserving the consistency of the prophetic tradition.
